service.name: Live music for a retirement party
service.serviceType: A jazz duo, a singer with a guitar, live band karaoke, a party band or a DJ for retirement parties thrown by a company or a family
service.description: Live music for a retirement party across Denver and the Front Range: a jazz duo playing the standards at 65 to 72 dBA under the dinner and silent for the speeches, a singer with a guitar who learns the retiree's song for the night, live band karaoke for the department, and a trio or quartet for the send-off that ends on a floor, at home, at a club, in a restaurant's private dining space or at the office, with an announcement microphone for the speeches, vendor paperwork where a company needs it, and one personal contact.

faqs.q: What are good retirement party ideas?
faqs.a: The retiree's song, the one they've requested at every office party for thirty years, learned for the night and sung with everyone watching; a set built from the standards and the songs of the year they started; live band karaoke, where the band plays the hits and hands the microphone to the colleagues; a jazz duo that goes silent for the speeches and comes back the moment the glass goes down; and a DJ or a band for the send-off that ends on a floor.

faqs.q: Can we hire a band for a retirement party?
faqs.a: Yes. The jazz duo or one guitarist is the size to price first, because the standards reach a table of colleagues aged twenty-five to seventy at once and the music has to get out of the way of the speeches. A singer with a guitar plays the retiree's song, live band karaoke gets the department singing, and a trio or a quartet plays the send-off that dances. It's one contract with one personal contact and an announcement microphone for whoever stands up.

faqs.q: Do you play retirement parties at the office, and can the company pay by purchase order?
faqs.a: Yes. A company's retirement dinner is a corporate booking with the same music, and vendor setup, a purchase order and a certificate of insurance are all available; none of them are fast, so start early. The corporate page covers vendor onboarding and how a band works around a program of speeches.

faqs.q: Can the band play the retiree's favorite song?
faqs.a: Yes. It's learned for the night if it isn't already in the book, and the first learned song is included in every booking. With live band karaoke, the retiring colleague's one karaoke song is a request we take the week before.

faqs.q: How does the music work around the speeches?
faqs.a: The band or the duo plays at 65 to 72 dBA at the nearest table, goes silent for the remarks and comes back the moment the glass goes down, and an announcement microphone is live for whoever stands up. Tell us roughly when the speeches fall and the set is built around them.

faqs.q: What does live music for a retirement party cost?
faqs.a: The pricing page sets out what live music costs in this market, and the cost guide has the Colorado figures for each kind of night. Tell us who's throwing it and where, because a company's dinner in a hotel function space and a family's dinner at home book different sizes, and we'll come back with a configuration and a price for the night.

faqs.q: How much space does the band need in a restaurant's private dining space?
faqs.a: One guitar takes 6 by 4 feet on one circuit, a duo 8 by 6 on one, a trio 12 by 8 on one, a quartet 14 by 10 on two, and live band karaoke 14 by 10 on two with its two lyric screens. Load-in runs 45 minutes for a solo and an hour for a duo or a trio, and we settle the load-in, the power and the volume with the venue before the day.
